instructions:
These tools drive the Windows PowerPoint desktop client through its COM automation interface, from WSL.
They read a deck's real geometry and text, add and change shapes on a 1280x720 px canvas by default,
render slides with PowerPoint itself, and save the result as .pptx.
Every length in the API is px at 96 dpi; PowerPoint's points are converted in the bridge.
Writes are two-step: the first call previews and returns an applyToken and a fingerprint; the second
call repeats the arguments with dryRun=false, that applyToken, and that expectFingerprint. A changed
deck is refused rather than overwritten. Nothing is saved until save_deck is called.
The server only closes presentations it opened or created; it never quits a PowerPoint the user had
already running.

tools.name: presentations
tools.title: Open presentations
tools.description: List the presentations PowerPoint currently has open, with their canvas size and slide count.

tools.name: read_deck
tools.title: Read a deck
tools.description: Read a deck's slides, shapes, text, geometry in px at 96 dpi, tables, charts, pictures and notes. Omit slides for a one-line-per-slide overview; pass slides (for example "1-3") to expand shapes. A path is opened read-only; a write tool reopens it editable when it has no unsaved changes.

presentation.description: Open presentation name or path. Omit when exactly one presentation is open.

tools.name: read_slide
tools.title: Read a slide
tools.description: Read one slide and its fingerprint. The fingerprint is what a write preview must still match.

presentation.description: Open presentation name or path. Omit when exactly one presentation is open.

tools.name: render
tools.title: Render slides
tools.description: Export slides as PNG files or the deck as a PDF, using PowerPoint's own renderer. outDir must be on a Windows drive. width/height apply to PNG; a PDF keeps the deck's page size. overwrite replaces existing files. The call ceiling is 55 s, so render large decks in slide batches.

presentation.description: Open presentation name or path. Omit when exactly one presentation is open.

outDir.description: Directory on a Windows drive, for example /mnt/c/Users/me/Temp/deck.

width.description: Output width in px for PNG; default 1600.

height.description: Output height in px for PNG; default 900.

tools.name: create_deck
tools.title: Create a deck
tools.description: Create a new presentation on a 1280x720 px canvas by default. theme accepts background, text, accent and font. Two steps: call it without dryRun first (nothing is written; the reply starts with an applyToken and a fingerprint), then call it again with the same arguments plus dryRun=false, that applyToken, and that expectFingerprint. A token is single use, expires after 10 minutes, and is bound to the exact arguments and to the deck state the preview saw.

path.description: Optional .pptx path on a Windows drive.

dryRun.description: Default true: preview only. Pass false, together with applyToken and expectFingerprint, to apply.

applyToken.description: The applyToken from the dry run of this same call. Required when dryRun is false.

expectFingerprint.description: The fingerprint from the dry run. Required when dryRun is false.

tools.name: add_slide
tools.title: Add a slide
tools.description: Add a slide with layout (blank, title, title-content, two-column, section), optional title, subtitle, position and background. Two steps: call it without dryRun first (nothing is written; the reply starts with an applyToken and a fingerprint), then call it again with the same arguments plus dryRun=false, that applyToken, and that expectFingerprint. A token is single use, expires after 10 minutes, and is bound to the exact arguments and to the deck state the preview saw.

presentation.description: Open presentation name or path. Omit when exactly one presentation is open.

layout.description: blank (default), title, title-content, two-column or section.

position.description: 1-based insertion position; default at the end.

dryRun.description: Default true: preview only. Pass false, together with applyToken and expectFingerprint, to apply.

applyToken.description: The applyToken from the dry run of this same call. Required when dryRun is false.

expectFingerprint.description: The fingerprint from the dry run. Required when dryRun is false.
